flows.what: Abbot Suger raised a large sum to rebuild the abbey church of Saint-Denis. He ordered the new choir in 1140. It opened in 1144 and is the first Gothic structure.
Guillaume Tirel, called Taillevent, served the Duke of Normandy from 1359. The duke became Charles V in 1364 and made him chief cook in 1373.

The wool guild of Florence held the patronage of the cathedral works from 1331. It ran the competition for the dome in 1418 and directed the work from 1420 to 1436. Public funds paid for the building.
Leonardo worked in Milan in the service of Ludovico Sforza. The page gives no payment figure for this period.
Pope Julius II commissioned Michelangelo to paint the Sistine Chapel ceiling. The contract of 8 May 1508 promised a fee of 3,000 ducats.
King Francis I took Leonardo into his service in France. He gave Leonardo the use of the manor Clos Lucé and a pension of 10,000 scudi in total.
An endowment from the French cardinal Matthieu Cointerel paid for the Contarelli Chapel in Rome. Caravaggio signed the contract for its paintings on 23 July 1599.
Marie de' Medici, widow of Henry IV, gave Rubens the commission for a cycle of paintings for the Luxembourg Palace. The price was about 24,000 guilders.
In 1662 Colbert bought the Gobelins works for Louis XIV. The site became a large furnishing workshop. Charles Le Brun ran it as director from 1663.
Louis XIV made Hardouin-Mansart his first architect at Versailles in 1678. He then built the Hall of Mirrors and the ministers' wings.
Louis XV bought the porcelain manufactory of Sèvres in 1759. Madame de Pompadour, its patron since 1751, kept free rein to run it.
Sir Nathaniel Curzon liked the garden temples of Robert Adam. In 1759 he commissioned the new mansion at Kedleston Hall and put Adam in charge.
Catherine the Great ordered the Frog Service of 952 pieces from Wedgwood in 1773. The Etruria Works made it, and she paid 2,700 pounds.
Rose Bertin met the queen in the summer of 1774 and made her coronation robes. She designed almost every new dress of the queen until 1792.
Carême worked as head pastry cook in the kitchens of Talleyrand at the Hôtel de Galliffet from 1803 to 1814.
Carême cooked for the Prince Regent, later George IV, at Carlton House and the Royal Pavilion. The salary was unusually high. No figure is known.
Paul Durand-Ruel met Monet in London in 1870. From 1872 he made large purchases of Impressionist paintings, among them a Monet.
Caillebotte bought his first Monet in 1875. He paid studio rent for Monet and bought works by Monet and other Impressionists.
Donors of the devotees of St Joseph paid for the Sagrada Família. Gaudí took charge of the project in 1883. No state or church body paid for it.
The industrialist Eusebi Güell commissioned the Palau Güell in Barcelona. Gaudí built it from 1886 to 1888.
The professor Emile Tassel was the client for the Hôtel Tassel in Brussels. Horta built it between 1892 and 1893.
For his first Cézanne show in 1895, Vollard bought almost the full output of the painter. This was about 150 canvases.
Anne Cobden-Sanderson paid for the Doves Press that her husband T. J. Cobden-Sanderson began. The infobox gives 1900 to 1916. The text says only that it began before 1900.
Fritz Waerndorfer financed the founding of the Wiener Werkstätte. The project used up his fortune. After the 1913 near-bankruptcy he left for America. Otto Primavesi took over as financier in 1914.
Gertrude and Leo Stein bought Matisse's Woman with a Hat soon after the Salon d'Automne of October 1905. Michael and Sarah Stein later bought many Matisse paintings.
The Steins bought Picasso's Young Girl with a Flower Basket in 1905. Gertrude kept the Picasso works after 1914 and went on to buy his Cubist paintings.
AEG retained Peter Behrens as artistic consultant. He designed its buildings, products and graphics. He stayed free to take other work.
Kahnweiler opened his gallery in 1907 and made contracts to buy all the work of some artists. His first purchases included Braque. The state seized the gallery in 1914.
Berthe Weill showed Fauve works in 1908 and 1909, among them works by Matisse, Derain and Braque.
Condé Montrose Nast bought Vogue in 1909, three years after the death of its founder. He made it a magazine for women. Circulation and profit grew.
Shchukin commissioned two large paintings from Matisse for his Moscow mansion. They were La Danse and Music, made in 1909 and 1910.
William Randolph Hearst bought Harper's Bazaar from Harper and Brothers in 1913. The magazine had lost money for years. Under Hearst it became a thick glossy magazine.
The German government, the War Ministry and Deutsche Bank gave the starting capital of UFA. UFA was privatised in 1921. The page names UFA as a leader of German Expressionism in the years after.
Paul Rosenberg had the first look at all new works of Picasso from 1918. No written contract existed. The deal ended in 1932.
The Social Democrat-led Thuringian government gave state support to the Bauhaus in Weimar. In 1924 a conservative ministry cut the funds in half.
Paul Rosenberg became the exclusive dealer of Braque in 1922. He gave early artists a secure income through exclusive buying contracts.
Albert Barnes bought Matisse's Le Bonheur de vivre in 1923 for 45,000 francs. He had bought his first two Matisse paintings from the Steins in 1912.
Condé Nast hired Edward Steichen as chief photographer of Vogue and Vanity Fair in 1923 for a salary of 35,000 dollars. He held the post until 1938.
After the success of the 1927 LaSalle, GM president Alfred P. Sloan formed the Art and Colour Section and made Harley Earl its first director.
DuPont hired Wallace Carothers to run pure research at its Experimental Station in 1928. His group made the polyamide that became nylon in 1935. His pay was 500 dollars a month.
Marie-Laure de Noailles and her husband paid for L'Âge d'Or, the film of Buñuel and Dalí, in 1930. The page gives no amount.
The Julien Levy Gallery in New York showed Dalí from 21 November to 8 December 1933. It held more Dalí shows in 1934, 1936, 1939 and 1941.
Edgar Kaufmann hired Wright in 1934 to design Fallingwater. The house and guest house cost 155,000 dollars, about four times the first budget.
The WPA Federal Art Project paid artists weekly wages. It treated abstract and figurative work alike. Pollock was one of the artists it supported before his work sold.
The Resettlement Administration, then the Farm Security Administration, then the Office of War Information ran a photography project under Roy Stryker. It made about 250,000 images.
The Resettlement Administration hired Dorothea Lange in 1935. Roy Stryker asked her to show the daily life of migrant workers.
In 1937 Edward James hosted Magritte in London for three weeks. He paid 250 pounds for copies of three paintings and gave him a studio.
Edward Weston won the first Guggenheim Fellowship ever given to a photographer. It paid 2,000 dollars for one year.
Edward James sponsored Salvador Dalí for all of 1938. The support lasted about two years in total. The page gives no amount.
Parliament passed the National Film Act on 2 May 1939 and created the NFB as a federal agency. Its Studio B unit made early cinéma vérité films.

sources.title: Wikipedia: National Film Board of Canada

flows.what: Dorothea Lange became the first woman to receive a Guggenheim Fellowship for photography. She gave it up after Pearl Harbor.
The Department of the Interior hired Ansel Adams for mural-size prints of parks. The contract ended 30 June 1942. The war stopped the murals.
Pollock signed a gallery contract with Peggy Guggenheim in July 1943. She also commissioned his Mural for her townhouse. Her gallery gave him a yearly stipend.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Art of This Century gallery

flows.what: Alexander Liberman offered Irving Penn a place in the art department of Vogue. Vogue printed his first photographic cover in October 1943. He worked for the magazine for the rest of his career.
Harper's Bazaar printed the first pages of Richard Avedon in October 1944, and then took him on as a staff photographer. Art director Alexey Brodovitch and editor Carmel Snow chose him.
Edith Farnsworth asked Mies to design a weekend house in 1945. It was finished in 1951. The cost was about 74,000 dollars, against a budget of 40,000.
George Nelson replaced Gilbert Rohde as design lead at Herman Miller. He brought in Isamu Noguchi, Charles and Ray Eames and Alexander Girard.
Ansel Adams used his first Guggenheim Fellowship to photograph the national parks. He got three fellowships in all.

Marcel Boussac backed the new Dior couture house on Avenue Montaigne. It started with a capital of 6 million francs, and his group Boussac Saint-Frères held the majority. Dior got one third of the pretax profit.
Walter Paepcke hired Herbert Bayer and moved him from New York to Aspen. Bayer also worked for the Container Corporation of America as design consultant.
The Charles Egan Gallery gave de Kooning his first one-man show in 1948. It showed his black and white paintings.
Howard Hughes spent 8.8 million dollars in May 1948 to take control of RKO. The studio had a house style of film noir.

The UK government paid for most of the Festival of Britain. The Council of Industrial Design promoted Good Design there. The lead of the source gives the cost as 12 million pounds; a later section gives 10.5 million.
Betty Parsons gave Barnett Newman his first solo show in 1950. She was the only dealer willing to take on artists such as Pollock after 1947.

The CIA paid for the Congress for Cultural Freedom until 1966. Frances Stonor Saunders says that the CIA promoted Abstract Expressionism through it. Michael Kimmelman calls much of that account false or without context.

sources.title: The Independent (1995): Modern art was CIA weapon
Kimmelman (1994): Revisiting the Revisionists, MoMA Studies in Modern Art 4

flows.what: The American High Commissioner John McCloy gave one million marks to the Ulm school project. Inge Scholl matched it with one million marks from industry and public bodies.
In 1952 Sidney Janis gave Pollock the first of three solo shows at his gallery. The gallery also represented Rothko and Kline.
Roger Vivier designed shoes for the house of Dior under contract. He made the modern stiletto heel in 1954 and the Aiguille and Choc heels in 1955. The sources differ on the end year: 1962 or 1963.
Alexander Plunket Greene bought Markham House on the King's Road in 1955 with Archie McNair. Mary Quant opened her Bazaar boutique there. He used an inheritance of 5,000 pounds.
Braun recruited Dieter Rams at age 23 as architect and interior designer. He became head of design at Braun six years later.
Max Miedinger drew Neue Haas Grotesk for the Haas Type Foundry under its head, Eduard Hoffmann. Hoffmann approved the final sample on 7 May 1957. The face became Helvetica.
Thomas J. Watson Jr. commissioned Eliot Noyes to build the first company-wide design programme at IBM. Noyes worked as consultant design director for about 21 years.
Knoll commissioned Eero Saarinen to design the Tulip chair for production. His Womb chair for Knoll dates from 1948.
The Ford Foundation sponsored a three-month tour of India by Charles and Ray Eames. Their India Report led to the National Institute of Design in 1961.
Jasper Johns joined the Leo Castelli Gallery in 1958. Castelli put his artists on a payroll, whether or not their work sold.
Rauschenberg joined the Leo Castelli Gallery in 1958. Castelli put his artists on a payroll, whether or not their work sold.
Georges de Beauregard produced Breathless. The budget was 400,000 francs. Filming ran from August to September 1959. Truffaut and Chabrol backed the idea.
Robert Venturi wrote most of Complexity and Contradiction in Architecture in 1962 under a grant from the Graham Foundation.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Complexity and Contradiction in Architecture

flows.what: After the Ferus Gallery show of 1962, Irving Blum bought all 32 Campbell's Soup Cans paintings for 1,000 dollars. He paid in ten monthly instalments of 100 dollars.
John and Dominique de Menil commissioned Rothko in 1964 to fill a meditation space with his paintings. The Rothko Chapel opened in 1971, after his death.
Garry Winogrand received Guggenheim Fellowships in 1964, 1969 and 1979. The first paid for studies of American life.
The Leo Castelli Gallery gave Warhol his first show there, Flowers, in November 1964.
Bertone hired Marcello Gandini at age 27 to replace Giorgetto Giugiaro. He designed the Lamborghini Miura in three months.
Castelli found Richard Serra in 1967. He offered him a guarantee of three years of monthly payments, with no hope of sales in that time.
Robert Adams received Guggenheim Fellowships in 1973 and 1980. He was part of New Topographics in 1975.
Robert Adams received an NEA Photographer's Fellowship in 1973 and another in 1978. He took part in New Topographics in 1975.
A National Endowment for the Arts fellowship paid for Stephen Shore's further work on Uncommon Places.
Stephen Shore received a Guggenheim Fellowship in 1975. It followed a 1974 NEA grant for Uncommon Places.
Warner Communications bought Atari from Nolan Bushnell for 28 million dollars in 1976. Under Warner, Atari released the VCS in 1977 and arcade hits such as Asteroids.
Philip Johnson won the Pritzker Architecture Prize in 1979. The Pritzker family funds the prize and the Hyatt Foundation sponsors it.
Warner-Amex Satellite Entertainment owned MTV when it began on 1 August 1981. The company had earlier commissioned the show PopClips.
Frank Gehry won the Pritzker Architecture Prize in 1989. The Pritzker family funds the prize and the Hyatt Foundation sponsors it.
Broderbund published Myst on 24 September 1993. The Miller brothers at Cyan made the game. It became the best selling title of Broderbund.
Renzo Piano won the Pritzker Architecture Prize in 1998. The Pritzker family funds the prize and the Hyatt Foundation sponsors it.
Hermès bought 35 percent of the Gaultier label for 150 million francs in 1999. Gaultier owned 93 percent before the deal. Hermès later raised its share to 45 percent.
Norman Foster won the Pritzker Architecture Prize in 1999. The Pritzker family funds the prize and the Hyatt Foundation sponsors it.
LVMH and Prada together bought 51 percent of Fendi in 1999. LVMH later bought the Prada share and 15.9 percent more. The sources give no LVMH amount for 1999.
Prada bought 51 percent of the New York company of Helmut Lang in March 1999. The company had a value of about 100 million US dollars.
Prada paid 105 million US dollars for full control of Jil Sander AG in 1999. Jil Sander left as chairwoman some months later.
Prada and LVMH together bought 51 percent of Fendi in October 1999. The Prada share was 25.5 percent. Prada sold it to LVMH under pressure from its banks.
Zaha Hadid won the Pritzker Architecture Prize in 2004. The Pritzker family funds the prize and the Hyatt Foundation sponsors it.
In 2005 the Nordic food ministers launched a New Nordic Food Programme. In 2006 this led to 3 million euros for related activities.

Google bought YouTube for 1.65 billion dollars in Google stock. It announced the deal on 9 October 2006 and closed it on 13 November 2006. The page lists vlogs among the main kinds of video on YouTube.
Richard Rogers won the Pritzker Architecture Prize in 2007. The Pritzker family funds the prize and the Hyatt Foundation sponsors it.
Tesla hired Franz von Holzhausen as chief designer. He led the design of the Model S, X, 3 and Y, the Semi and the Cybertruck.
The Pebble watch campaign ran from 11 April to 18 May 2012. It reached its first goal of 100,000 dollars in two hours. 68,929 backers pledged 10,266,845 dollars.
Charles River Ventures put 15 million dollars into Pebble as a Series A round in 2013. Before that, Eric Migicovsky had raised 375,000 dollars from angel investors.
Microsoft agreed to buy Mojang for 2.5 billion dollars on 15 September 2014. The sale closed on 6 November 2014. Mojang then joined Xbox Game Studios.
The Pebble Time campaign ran from 24 February to 27 March 2015. 78,471 backers pledged 20,338,986 dollars. The page ranks it among the top Kickstarter campaigns.
Microsoft put 1 billion dollars into OpenAI in 2019. OpenAI moved its services to Microsoft Azure. ChatGPT came out in November 2022.
TikTok announced its Creator Fund on 22 July 2020. It started with 200 million dollars for creators in the US, paid out over one year. TikTok said it expected the fund to grow.

sources.title: TikTok Newsroom: Introducing the 200 million dollar TikTok Creator Fund

flows.what: YouTube set up a fund of 100 million dollars in August 2021 to pay top creators of Shorts. It spread the money over 2021 and 2022. YouTube called it a stopgap.
Microsoft announced a further 10 billion dollars for OpenAI on 23 January 2023, over several years. Much of it paid for Azure compute. The page puts the value of OpenAI at 29 billion dollars.
